summary: Ephemeral service-account provisioning failing due to IAM condition time-window rejection
description: Issue summary: Automated ephemeral service-account provisioning (JIT) used by the Dedicated provisioner is intermittently failing during STS/session creation. Impact: onboarding/provisioning flows for internal tooling and some Dedicated customer onboarding jobs are stuck; CI jobs that rely on ephemeral SA keys fail, causing rollout delays. Observed error is an IAM condition rejection referencing a time-window condition. This appears to affect only a subset of requests and correlates with transient clock skew and a recently tightened IAM condition on the 'provisioner-broker' service role.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Run the ephemeral provisioning job: tools/provisioner/jit-create --project=dedicated-prod --env=staging-proxy
2) Observe the broker attempt to assume the target service role via STS (gcp->aws federated path)
3) Provisioner logs show 403/ConditionNotMet returned by IAM when evaluating a condition expression containing request.time comparison
4) Re-run the same job: some attempts succeed, others fail (non-deterministic).
logs:
2026-03-10T15:22:41Z ERROR broker: sts-assume failed, error=ConditionNotMet: Condition (request.time < timestamp('2026-03-10T15:22:30Z')) not satisfied. request_id=abc123
2026-03-10T15:22:41Z DEBUG broker: token creation attempted with now=2026-03-10T15:22:41Z
Audit log (GCP): principalEmail=provisioner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com protoPayload.methodName=SetIamPolicy protoPayload.status.code=7 conditionEvaluation=false
Stacktrace: tools/provisioner/broker/assume.go:142
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: tightened IAM condition was deployed in org-policy update on 2026-03-09 to restrict provisioner tokens to a narrow time-window; side effect: clock skew between hosted provisioner and auth validators causes ConditionNotMet. Evidence: failed requests show request.time outside the allowed timestamp range; successful requests have request.time within. We reproduced by artificially shifting the provisioner system clock forward/back and observed failures/successes. Correlated with a change in repo infra/iam/policies/2026-03-09 that added a hard-coded timestamp window for temporary SA issuance. Also found a handful of related 403s in cloud-audit logs with same condition id. Possible root causes: (A) overly strict hard-coded time window in IAM condition, (B) provisioner uses cert-based short-lived tokens with slight clock skew, (C) STS/GCP evaluation expects RFC3339 exactness and we supply a different granularity.
comments: 2026-03-10 16:05 - Kaitlyn Moore: Noted same failures on a Dedicated onboarding job (job-id: ded-onb-1122) around 15:20Z. Added provisioning logs to the ticket.

2026-03-10 17:00 - Evan Kim: Reproduced locally by setting local clock +25s. When request.time is ahead of condition upper bound the call is rejected with ConditionNotMet. Raising to infra for immediate rollback option.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Joao Ribeiro (Infra): We pushed a quick revert to infra/iam/policies/commit@f7a1b that removed the hard-coded upper bound. Observed provisioning success for a 30m window after revert. Still monitoring for residual failures.

2026-03-12 11:34 - Security: Recommend follow-up to replace hard-coded timestamps with relative conditions (e.g., request.time < request.auth.token_issue_time + duration) where possible; also request NTP compliance checks on fleet nodes.
2026-03-12 12:02 - Evan Kim: Adding follow-up tasks and marking remediation in progress.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Reverted the change that introduced the hard-coded upper time bound in the IAM condition (infra/iam/policies rollback commit f7a1b). Immediate effect: provisioning success rate returned to baseline. Permanent fix: replace fixed timestamp conditions with duration-based conditions and add test coverage for condition evaluation under clock skew. Deployment notes: patch to policies implemented in canary org, then rolled to prod after 24h monitoring.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Add unit/integration tests that emulate clock skew against IAM conditions. 2) Enforce NTP/chrony checks in provisioner deployment jobs. 3) Replace static timestamp conditions with relative logic across all org-level IAM policies. 4) Create runbook entry for diagnosing ConditionNotMet during ephemeral SA creation.
